newsitem.title: TURKEY: Inmates at several Turkish prisons join protest.
newsitem.headline: Inmates at several Turkish prisons join protest.

text.p: Prisoners at several Turkish prisons have held protests in solidarity with inmates at a jail in western Turkey where clashes with guards have left five injured, human rights officials said on Tuesday.
Four guards and one gendarme were taken to hospital after the initial protest at Buca jail on Monday. A prison guard taken hostage there has since been set free, officials said.

In response to this protest, inmates at prisons in Umraniye in Istanbul, Bursa and Bergama in western Turkey took guards hostage on Monday night, according to Ercan Demir, Izmir representative of the Turkish Human Rights Association (IHD).
Demir said 23 prison officials taken hostage in Umraniye have been set free, as have eight guards in Bursa. One guard at Bergama prison remained hostage to inmates.

Human rights officials say relations between the prison guards and inmates at Buca prison had worsened since guards carried out a search for a suspected escape tunnel in February. Buca houses many leftist and Kurdish rebel prisoners.
Izmir Bar Association chairman Cetin Turan told Reuters inmates at Buca continued to occupy the exercise yard. There was no confirmation of earlier reports that prisoners had been injured.
Firefighters on Monday extinguished a fire there which apparently broke out in a section of the prison holding members of the left-wing guerrilla group Dev Sol, witnesses said.
Turan and IHD representatives visited the prison at the request of the prison governor to negotiate between the inmates and the prison authorities.
"We talked with the prisoners in front of the barricades. They said they were not out to take hostages," Turan said.
"They set the guard free and the prison authorities pulled the soldiers back. There was an easing of tension. At the moment there are no new developments," he said.
